key_claims: DPIaC-Eval: LLM IaC evaluation usually checks syntax, not whether templates deploy. Six LLMs deploy only about 20.8-30.2% first attempt. IaCGen (iterative feedback: format, syntax, live deployment) raises deployability. Generated templates score poorly on user intent (25.2%) and security compliance (8.4%). OPA docs: OPA/Conftest can enforce policy-as-code guardrails in CI/CD, failing the pipeline by exit code (--fail, --fail-defined), and unit-test Terraform plans (terraform show -json then opa exec). Fu et al.: static analysis of Copilot/CodeWhisperer/Codeium snippets in real GitHub projects flagged 733 snippets across 43 CWEs; feeding analyzer warnings to Copilot Chat fixed up to 55.5% of issues (19.3% with plain fix command).
headline_figures: LEAD DOES NOT MATCH. The lead says 'DPIaC-Eval shows 91.6% of AI-generated IaC fails baseline security checks on first pass'. Wrong. 91.6% is the top end of the deployable rate (Claude-3.5, pItr@10 in Table 2) after IaCGen iterative feedback within 10 iterations, range 54.6-91.6%. It is a success rate, not a failure rate, and not about security. Security figure is 8.4% 'full compliance' (Filtered Compliance Rate, excludes templates with no applicable policies), measured with Checkov, not OPA. That implies roughly 91.6% non-compliant, but the paper does not state that, and it is across generated templates not 'first pass'; the numerical coincidence is likely the source of the garbled lead. Do not use '91.6% fails security'. Other numbers: first-attempt deployment 20.8-30.2%; intent coverage 25.2%; 153 scenarios, 58 AWS services, five difficulty levels; models GPT-4o, GPT-o3-mini, Claude-3.5, Claude-3.7, DeepSeek-R1, DeepSeek-V3. Fu et al.: 733 snippets; 29.5% Python, 24.2% JavaScript; 43 CWEs; 55.5% fixed with enhanced prompt. 4,241 CWE instances in 7,703 files across 77 types is from a separate 2025 arXiv study (2510.26103) seen only in a search snippet. [uncertain]
sample_and_method: DPIaC-Eval: 153 AWS CloudFormation tasks (Terraform only in a small syntax-only generalizability test on IaC-Eval, 79.7% passItr@1), live deployment validation, Checkov for security policies; observed, not self-reported. Fu et al.: real-world GitHub projects, Copilot-attributed snippets analysed with static analysis tools (tool names unconfirmed), then Copilot Chat repair experiment.
limitations: DPIaC-Eval stated: model currency (older models), benchmark coverage, difficulty categorisation, not all IaC languages. Visible: CloudFormation only; no OPA/Rego evidence; the 8.4% is a filtered rate on Checkov's built-in policies; benchmark tasks, not production PRs; no measure of human review load. Fu et al.: snippet-level static analysis, false positives not resolved in what I read, no measure of reviewer time saved; the weakness rate shifted between versions (earlier preprint 35.8%). Neither source measures whether gates reduce review burden. No primary source found or opened that shows an OPA/Rego gate blocking unencrypted S3 at plan time; OPA docs pages opened contain no S3 or encryption example, so that lead is unsupported by these pages.
what_a_leader_can_do: Supports: automate objective checks (deployability, policy compliance, static analysis) in CI so humans review intent and design. Evidence moderate for the idea that AI IaC needs policy gates (8.4% compliance, Checkov) and that feeding analyzer output back to the model improves fixes (55.5%, Fu et al.). Weak for the claim that gates cut human review load: not measured. Use OPA docs only for 'policy-as-code guardrails can run in CI', not for the S3 example.
overlap_with_site_essays: High with Checking Isn't Catching and The Verification Gap (deterministic checks versus judgement); moderate with What It Takes to Trust Agent Output (gates as a trust mechanism); low with Overseeing Agents Is the Tiring Part.
